name: ghc_campaign_local_session
status: source updated for strict Clockwork drill API validation; GSC compile/round-trip and binary identity pending CI; not injected or runtime-tested
behavior: Reuses only engine-created native split-screen players; validates the exact live primary/secondary pair against the current player entity array before session reuse and Campaign actions; centralized invalidation sets status 8, releases active drill/event locks, rebuilds the original level.playerpiggyback array from live player entities, preserves the previous primary when still present (otherwise the first live player), and clears stale secondary aliases; the Clockwork drill ownership helper allows one global active owner at a time and requires Stage 1 completion before Stage 2; owner may change between stages; exposes Player 2 loadout helper; never spawns or clones a player. Adds a single guarded lifecycle watcher after a successful or failed initial bind; the watcher retries binding an already-existing native pair from a fresh engine player array every 250 ms and invalidates/releases active ownership after eight consecutive failed checks. A new main() call during a pending stop waits for the existing watcher to exit before touching aliases or starting a replacement; if the old watcher does not exit within two seconds, startup returns fail-closed. The start-monitor helper refuses to create a second watcher while the previous watcher is stopping. Explicit monitor shutdown invalidates a ready session, releases active drill/event locks, preserves completed event history, restores the original Campaign player array and clears stale secondary aliases. The monitor remains the single lifecycle owner and never creates or clones a player. Initializes the reusable 16-ID shared mission event lock after native-pair validation and aborts active event locks on rebind or stale-session invalidation while preserving completed mission events. The event-lock release API rejects an undefined or non-boolean completion flag; only exact numeric 0 or 1 is accepted. The Clockwork drill begin/finish API rejects undefined or out-of-range spot IDs; finish requires an explicit numeric completion flag of exactly 0 or 1, and the shared completion-state setter validates both slot and boolean values before mutation.
